title: Epistle to the Romans
context: These blocks come from Paul's Epistle to the Romans in the Westcott-Hort Greek New Testament: a Koine Greek letter of theological argument, with long periods, dense chains of prepositional phrases and genitives, rhetorical questions, and quotation of the Septuagint. Some opening words are printed in capitals in this edition; interpret them by meaning. Render theologically loaded terms such as δικαιοσύνη, πίστις, νόμος, and σάρξ by their sense in context, consistently, without importing a particular doctrinal interpretation. Keep the structure of long periods visible in literal translations, and divide them naturally in prose without losing any clause. Do not reproduce the wording of a particular English Bible.
